source_text:
Ὃ ἐάν τις καθ̓ ἓν ἕκαστον εἰλικρινῶς κατανοήσῃ, ἐπιγνώσεται μεγαλεῖα τῶν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ δεδομένων δωρεῶν.
ἐξ αὐτοῦ γὰρ ἱερεῖς καὶ Λευῖται πάντες οἱ λειτουργοῦντες τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ τοῦ θεοῦ: ἐξ αὐτοῦ ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς τὸ κατὰ σάρκα. ἐξ αὐτοῦ βασιλεῖς καὶ ἄρχοντες καὶ ἡγούμενοι κατὰ τὸν Ἰούδαν: τὰ δὲ λοιπὰ σκῆπτρα αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἐν μικρᾷ δόξῃ ὑπάρχουσιν, ὡς ἐπαγγειλαμένου τοῦ θεοῦ, ὅτι ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου ὡς οἱ ἀστέρες τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
πάντες οὖν ἐδοξάσθησαν καὶ ἐμεγαλύνθησαν οὐ δἰ αὐτῶν ἢ τῶν ἔργων αὐτῶν ἢ τῆς δικαιοπραγίας ἧς κατειργάσαντο, ἀλλὰ διὰ τοῦ θελήματος αὐτοῦ.
καὶ ἡμεῖς οὖν, διὰ θελήματος αὐτοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ κληθέντες, οὐ δἰ ἑαυτῶν δικαιούμεθα, οὐδὲ διὰ τῆς ἡμετέρας σοφίας ἢ συνέσεως ἢ εὐσεβείας ἢ ἔργων ὦν κατειργασάμεθα ἐν ὁσιότητι καρδίας, ἀλλὰ διὰ τῆς πίστεως, δἰ ἦς πάντας τοὺς ἀπ’ αἰῶνος ʽ??ʼ παντοκράτωρ θεὸς ἐδικαίωσεν: ᾧ ἔστω ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. ἀμήν.
thought_title: All gifts and justification come from God's will, not from ourselves
orientation: The Roman church is writing to the Corinthian church, and here it is concluding its long survey of God's blessings from Abraham through Jacob by drawing the lesson that every gift and every justification comes from God's will alone.
pass_a_gloss: If anyone considers each one of these things sincerely, he will recognize the great things of the gifts given by him. For from him are priests and all the Levites who minister at the altar of God; from him is the Lord Jesus according to the flesh. From him are kings and rulers and leaders according to Judah; and the rest of his scepters are not in small glory, since God promised that your seed will be as the stars of heaven. All therefore were glorified and made great not through themselves or their works or the righteous deeds which they accomplished, but through his will. And we therefore, having been called through his will in Christ Jesus, are not justified through ourselves, nor through our wisdom or understanding or piety or works which we accomplished in holiness of heart, but through the faith, through which the almighty God justified all those from eternity; to whom be the glory forever and ever. Amen.

choices.why: The literal image of royal scepters is kept, since the passage is listing the honors that came from Jacob's line; 'tribes' would lose the royal connotation that pairs with kings, rulers, and leaders.
The compound noun means the doing of righteous acts, and 'righteous deeds' preserves the active sense of accomplished works, which the passage is contrasting with God's will.
The phrase is kept literal to preserve the inner disposition being denied as a ground of justification.
The phrase means all people from the beginning of time, and 'from eternity' keeps the temporal sweep of God's justifying work.
The standard rendering of the divine title, kept as a fixed epithet.

bible_refs.note: ὅτι ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου ὡς οἱ ἀστέρες τοῦ οὐρανοῦ

pass_b_english: If anyone considers each of these things with a sincere mind, he will recognize the greatness of the gifts given by him.

For from Jacob came the priests and all the Levites who minister at the altar of God. From him came the Lord Jesus according to the flesh. From him came kings and rulers and leaders in the line of Judah, and the rest of his scepters are in no small glory, because God promised, “Your descendants will be like the stars of the sky” (Genesis 22:17).
All of them, then, were glorified and magnified not through themselves or their works or the righteous deeds they accomplished, but through God’s will.

So we too, called through God’s will in Christ Jesus, are not justified through ourselves, nor through our own wisdom or understanding or piety or works done in holiness of heart, but through faith, by which almighty God has justified all those from eternity. To him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
notes: The source text contains a damaged or uncertain passage marked ʽ??ʼ after ἀπ’ αἰῶνος; the gloss renders only what is legible and does not supply missing text.

problems.why: Source pronoun refers back to God (τῶν ὑπ' αὐτοῦ δεδομένων δωρεῶν), not Jacob.
problems.fix: For from him came the priests and all the Levites who minister at the altar of God.

edits.old: For from Jacob came the priests and all the Levites who minister at the altar of God.
edits.new: For from him came the priests and all the Levites who minister at the altar of God.

problems.quote: For from God came the priests and all the Levites who minister at the altar of God. From God came the Lord Jesus according to the flesh. From God came kings and rulers
problems.source_quote: ἐξ αὐτοῦ γὰρ ἱερεῖς καὶ Λευῖται πάντες
problems.why: αὐτοῦ refers back to Jacob (section 31), not God. The English makes God the source of priests, Christ's flesh and kings, which changes the claim. The ancestry runs through Jacob.
problems.fix: For from him (Jacob) came the priests and all the Levites who minister at the altar of God. From him came the Lord Jesus according to the flesh. From him came kings and rulers and leaders in the line of Judah.

problems.quote: the rest of his scepters are in no small glory
problems.why: With 'God' as the earlier subject, 'his' reads as God's scepters. The source means Jacob's remaining tribal scepters.
problems.fix: and his remaining scepters (the other tribes) are held in no small glory

problems.quote: the greatness of the gifts God has given
problems.source_quote: μεγαλεῖα τῶν ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ δεδομένων δωρεῶν
problems.why: αὐτοῦ is Jacob, the antecedent from the examples just given, not God.
problems.fix: the greatness of the gifts given by him
problems.ruling: ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ is 'by him', the same Jacob as ἐξ αὐτοῦ in the next sentence (priests, Levites, Judah). The English inserts 'God' for the pronoun.

problems.quote: From God came the Lord Jesus according to the flesh.
problems.source_quote: ἐξ αὐτοῦ ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς τὸ κατὰ σάρκα
problems.why: “According to the flesh” is human descent from Jacob, not origin from God.
problems.fix: From him came the Lord Jesus according to the flesh.
problems.ruling: ἐξ αὐτοῦ ... τὸ κατὰ σάρκα means descent from Jacob, with the Levites and Judah's line. 'From God came the Lord Jesus according to the flesh' misstates the lineage.

edits.old: he will recognize the greatness of the gifts God has given.
edits.new: he will recognize the greatness of the gifts given by him.

edits.old: For from God came the priests and all the Levites who minister at the altar of God. From God came the Lord Jesus according to the flesh. From God came kings and rulers and leaders in the line of Judah,
edits.new: For from Jacob came the priests and all the Levites who minister at the altar of God. From him came the Lord Jesus according to the flesh. From him came kings and rulers and leaders in the line of Judah,

fixed: Fixed priests/kings ancestry: ἐξ αὐτοῦ ... ἐξ αὐτοῦ ... ἐξ αὐτοῦ refers to Jacob, so changed threefold 'From God came' to 'From Jacob ... From him ... From him'.
No separate edit for scepters: τὰ δὲ λοιπὰ σκῆπτρα αὐτοῦ is Jacob's, and after the ancestry fix 'his' now unambiguously reads as Jacob's, so the current wording is correct.
Fixed gift-giver: ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ δεδομένων refers to Jacob as in ἐξ αὐτοῦ γάρ, so changed 'gifts God has given' to 'gifts given by him'.
Fixed Christ's descent: ἐξ αὐτοῦ ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς τὸ κατὰ σάρκα is descent from Jacob, covered by the same ancestry edit to 'From him came the Lord Jesus according to the flesh'.

polish.changed: Clarified that the repeated 'from him' refers to God, made the subject of each sentence explicit, and smoothed the flow for reading aloud while preserving every claim and quotation.
